Q116274072.summary: On this fragment of carved tusk Christ sits frontally within an oval mandorla studded with ring-and-dot ornament, bearded and haloed, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a book in his left. Below him a winged angel reclines, appearing to support the mandorla. The stylised, patterned carving is characteristic of ivory work from early Islamic Egypt, where Christian communities continued to produce images of Christ in glory.
facts: The Met dates the fragment to 810–1010 and attributes it to Egypt (accession 17.190.48, gift of J. Pierpont Morgan, 1917).
It is held in The Met's Department of Islamic Art, like the related tusk fragment with the Ascension (17.190.46), which shows a very similar enthroned Christ in a dotted mandorla.
Q116274072.notes: The relationship between the two Met tusk fragments is noted from their shared style, department and gift; whether they come from the same object was not verified.
